verdict.rationale: Figma exposes several programmatic surfaces. The REST API reads any objects, layers and properties, offers full CRUD on variables, and manages webhooks. The Plugin API gives read/write access to create and modify file contents, and the MCP server lets agents write native content to the canvas. However, the REST API is described mainly as view/extract, and full write access sits in the Plugin API, which runs inside the editor when a user invokes it. Nothing documents that every UI action has an API equivalent, so parity is incomplete. Missing for 10: headless REST write access to arbitrary canvas content, documented API coverage for UI features like prototyping, version history and comments, and independent evidence of UI/API parity.
